newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuba says army should be alert before US election.
newsitem.headline: Cuba says army should be alert before US election.

text.p: A senior Cuban general said on Thursday the armed forces should be vigilant and alert until after the Nov. 5 U.S. presidential election because Washington was not ruling out a "military attack" on Cuba.

The official news agency Prensa Latina quoted armed forces chief of staff Gen. Ulises Rosales as telling young soldiers in Havana preparedness of the public and armed forces should be a warning "to the enemy, so that nobody makes a mistake and tries to win votes with a military provocation against Cuba."
There has been no indication in the United States that President Bill Clinton is planning any sort of military action against Cuba.

Cuba and the United States have had hostile relations since the 1959 revolution that brought President Fidel Castro to power. Washington reinforced its longstanding economic embargo against the island in the wake of the shooting down by Cuban fighters in February of two small private U.S. planes.

Prensa Latina quoted Rosales as saying Washington had toughened its economic measures against Cuba and did not rule out military action, as recent press reports had shown. The Miami Herald newspaper reported several weeks ago that at the time of the plane downings a military attack was one option considered by U.S. authorities as a reprisal measure.

Cuba argued it shot down the Cuban exile-operated planes because they were violating its airspace. But Washington, which led international condemnation of the incident, said the planes were over international waters. The four crew members were killed in the incident.
